prompt: Why are two indirect methods usually used to hydrate alkenes in the laboratory?

choices.text: Direct hydration with aqueous acid is generally a poor laboratory reaction
Alkenes don't react with water under any conditions at all
choices.why: Acid-catalyzed hydration does happen; it's just generally a poor reaction in the laboratory.

choices.text: The indirect methods are the only way to make 1,2-diols from alkenes
choices.why: Hydroboration–oxidation and oxymercuration–demercuration give simple alcohols. 1,2-Diols come from OsO4 or epoxide hydrolysis.

choices.text: Direct hydration requires OsO4, which is too expensive to use
choices.why: OsO4 is used to make 1,2-diols, not for simple hydration.

explanation: Because the direct hydration of alkenes with aqueous acid is generally a poor reaction in the laboratory, two indirect methods are commonly used: hydroboration–oxidation and oxymercuration–demercuration.

prompt: Which statement correctly compares the two indirect alkene hydration methods?

choices.text: Hydroboration–oxidation gives the syn, non-Markovnikov product; oxymercuration–demercuration gives the Markovnikov product
Hydroboration–oxidation gives the Markovnikov product; oxymercuration–demercuration gives the non-Markovnikov product
choices.why: The two are swapped. Hydroboration–oxidation is the non-Markovnikov method.

choices.text: Both give the Markovnikov product, but only hydroboration–oxidation is syn
choices.why: Hydroboration–oxidation puts the –OH on the less substituted carbon, the non-Markovnikov result.

choices.text: Both give the non-Markovnikov product, but only oxymercuration–demercuration is syn
choices.why: Oxymercuration–demercuration gives the Markovnikov product, and it's hydroboration that is described as syn.

explanation: Hydroboration–oxidation yields the syn, non-Markovnikov hydration product (Section 8.5), whereas oxymercuration–demercuration yields the Markovnikov hydration product (Section 8.4).

prompt: What product forms when 1-methylcyclohexene is treated with BH3, followed by H2O2?

choices.why: That is the Markovnikov product, which oxymercuration–demercuration gives.
H and OH add to the same face (syn), so the –OH ends up trans to the methyl group.
A diol needs OsO4. Hydroboration–oxidation adds only one –OH group.

explanation: Hydroboration–oxidation is a syn, non-Markovnikov hydration. The –OH goes to the less substituted carbon (carbon 2), and the H added to carbon 1 is on the same face as the –OH, which leaves the methyl and –OH trans: trans-2-methylcyclohexanol, formed in 84% yield.

prompt: What product forms when 1-methylcyclohexene is treated with mercuric acetate in water, followed by NaBH4?

choices.why: That is the non-Markovnikov product, which hydroboration–oxidation gives.
Oxymercuration–demercuration is a Markovnikov hydration, so the –OH goes to the more substituted carbon, the one bearing the methyl group.
NaBH4 replaces the mercury with hydrogen; the –OH that came from water stays, so the product is an alcohol.

explanation: Oxymercuration–demercuration gives the Markovnikov hydration product, placing the –OH on the more substituted double-bond carbon. 1-Methylcyclohexene gives 1-methylcyclohexanol in 90% yield.

choices.text: Oxymercuration–demercuration (mercuric acetate in water, then NaBH4)
choices.why: This Markovnikov method puts the –OH on the more substituted carbon, giving 2-methyl-2-propanol.
This adds an –OH to both double-bond carbons, giving a 1,2-diol.
Epoxidation followed by acid-catalyzed hydrolysis also gives a 1,2-diol, not a simple alcohol.

explanation: 2-Methyl-1-propanol has its –OH on the less substituted carbon of the former double bond, the non-Markovnikov result. Hydroboration–oxidation gives the non-Markovnikov product; oxymercuration–demercuration would give 2-methyl-2-propanol.

prompt: What does a cycloalkene give when treated with OsO4 followed by NaHSO3, and why?

choices.text: A cis-1,2-diol, because the reaction occurs with syn stereochemistry
A trans-1,2-diol, because the reaction occurs with anti stereochemistry
choices.why: That describes acid-catalyzed opening of an epoxide, not OsO4 hydroxylation.

choices.text: A cis-1,2-diol, because the reaction occurs with anti stereochemistry
choices.why: Anti addition to a ring gives a trans diol. OsO4 adds with syn stereochemistry.

choices.text: A single alcohol with Markovnikov orientation
choices.why: OsO4 adds two –OH groups, one to each double-bond carbon.

explanation: 1,2-Diols can be made by direct hydroxylation of an alkene with OsO4 followed by reduction with NaHSO3. The OsO4 reaction occurs with syn stereochemistry, so a cycloalkene gives a cis diol.

prompt: 1-Methylcyclohexene is treated with a peroxyacid in CH2Cl2, and the epoxide formed is then hydrolyzed with aqueous acid. What kind of product results?

choices.text: A trans-1,2-diol, from anti opening of the epoxide
A cis-1,2-diol, from syn opening of the epoxide
choices.why: Epoxide opening occurs with anti stereochemistry. The cis diol comes from OsO4.
Epoxide hydrolysis puts an –OH on both former double-bond carbons, not just one.
Epoxide hydrolysis gives a 1,2-diol, with –OH groups on both former double-bond carbons.

explanation: Acid-catalyzed hydrolysis of an epoxide is the second route to 1,2-diols. Epoxide opening occurs with anti stereochemistry, so the cyclic alkene gives a trans diol, while OsO4 gives the cis diol.

prompt: What alcohol forms when 2-methyl-2-pentene, (CH3)2C=CHCH2CH3, is treated with BH3 and then with NaOH and H2O2?

choices.why: That is the Markovnikov product, with the –OH on the more substituted carbon. Hydroboration–oxidation gives the non-Markovnikov product.
The –OH goes on one of the double-bond carbons (carbon 2 or 3). Carbon 1 isn't part of the double bond.
A diol needs OsO4. Hydroboration–oxidation adds only one –OH group.

explanation: Hydroboration–oxidation is non-Markovnikov: the –OH goes to the less substituted double-bond carbon. In (CH3)2C=CHCH2CH3 that is carbon 3, giving (CH3)2CHCH(OH)CH2CH3, 2-methyl-3-pentanol (Exercise 17.3.1).

prompt: What forms when 2-methyl-4-phenyl-1-butene, H2C=C(CH3)CH2CH2C6H5, is treated with mercuric acetate in water and then NaBH4?

choices.why: That non-Markovnikov product would come from hydroboration–oxidation.
A 1,2-diol needs OsO4 or epoxide hydrolysis. Oxymercuration–demercuration adds a single –OH.
NaBH4 replaces the mercury with hydrogen; the –OH that came from water stays.

explanation: Oxymercuration–demercuration gives the Markovnikov product: the –OH goes to the more substituted double-bond carbon, carbon 2. The product, (CH3)2C(OH)CH2CH2C6H5, is 2-methyl-4-phenyl-2-butanol (Exercise 17.3.1).

prompt: What forms when (Z)-5-decene, cis-CH3(CH2)3CH=CH(CH2)3CH3, is treated with OsO4 and then NaHSO3 in water?

choices.why: That pair would come from anti addition to the Z alkene. OsO4 adds with syn stereochemistry, and syn addition to a cis alkene gives the meso diol.
OsO4 adds two –OH groups, one to each double-bond carbon, not one.
OsO4 hydroxylation keeps the carbon chain intact. It doesn't cleave the double bond.

explanation: OsO4 hydroxylation occurs with syn stereochemistry. Syn addition of two –OH groups to the cis double bond of (Z)-5-decene gives meso-5,6-decanediol (Exercise 17.3.1).
